utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Earlier you described the liberation of a territory, when I asked you about liberation, as these are the words you used, "freeing of territory taken from the enemy." That's what you said earlier this morning.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Meaning the capture of territory -- the capture of territory from an enemy? Meaning land.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Territory, land, yes, that's what it means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The capture of territory in the Bosanski Samac municipality by the paramilitaries and others could not have been or was not a positive liberation for the non-Serb majority that was living there, was it?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will say no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And everyone on the 2nd Posavina Brigade who signed the document you had there earlier, that's P127, including yourself, was aware that this liberation, being the capture of territory taken from the enemy, was not a positive liberation for non-Serbs; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you signed that document, you were all aware, all of you, every one of you who signed that document, that there was no positive liberation of that territory from the non-Serbs; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, but we didn't know in which direction this would go. The resettlement, transfer, arrests, this is what I'm talking about, in the previous period none of us knew how it would go.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown P127 ter?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you said in the previous period. You signed the document in November or December, 1992, and it sets outs in great detail a lot of the horrific things that had been happening in Bosanski Samac since the 17th of April, and you've agreed those things were committed by Crisis Staff and paramilitary on ethnic, that is discriminatory, grounds.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at that point, it was obvious that the direction in which things were going was not a positive one for the non-Serbs who had been arrested, detained, tortured, had their possessions looted from them, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. And it wasn't even positive for the people in my detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I want you to turn to -- I'm not quite sure if you have the same page number as I do -- could you just tell me to assist, how many pages do you have on that document? I have ten on my English translation. How many do you have?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ten, ten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first page, please, the third paragraph or maybe it's the fourth paragraph. Do you see the words, "This group played"? You see a paragraph headed "first," and then there is a paragraph headed "second." There is a paragraph headed "third." In between second and third.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have those indications here but I will try to find it in the text, if you just give me a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where I want you to go to is in the part under "second" can you see the words Todorovic and Mijak?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Immediately under that, is the sentence, "This group" that's referring to the paramilitaries above, "Played an indisputably positive role in the liberation of Samac as a part of the Special Battalion" and it goes on to say, "In fighting at Vidovice, Kornica, Garevac and Kladari, in the liberation of the corridor to Brcko," and so on. You see the words, "This group played an indisputably positive role in the liberation of Samac as part of the Special Battalion"? My question is: Do you see the words there?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what you've just said and the questions and answers in the last few minutes, what that really means, doesn't it, is this group played an indisputably positive role in the military takeover on ethnic grounds of Bosanski Samac and the installation of a Serb-only government? That's really what it means, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is calling for speculation, what they meant. It is quite obvious what it says in the information. They were -- I mean from the paragraph that my learned colleague has just read that as a member of Special Battalion that there is this sentence also so --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The witness has already answered yes and he's an author of the document. He signed the document. He's already said yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The word liberation occurs twice more in this document. I'm just -- if you turn to the page where it says -- the second page where it says, "Fifth, the fact that criminals of a Yugoslav calibre were hiding among the 'Serbian commandos' who had come to train the Serbian people it was revealed by their behaviour a few days after the liberation of Samac." You see that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you found it? Have you read it? I just want you to indicate whether you've read it and whether I read out correctly what it says.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You would have to repeat that to me.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, could the document please be placed on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are talking about the text, then I agree this is a part of the text, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, turn to the sixth page, could you possibly put it on the ELMO? That's the --

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me it's easier this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think the witness wants -- can only read it if it's before him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you lean to your left and read that there? Is it possible? Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. About a third of the way down the page, in brackets, after the brackets, "The fate of hard currency acquired in this way should be explained. What I want to you concentrate on is what is suggested by the disappearance of a huge quantity of weapons collected during the liberation of Samac and some other places populated by Croats. Especially hunting weapons, which disappeared over night and were transported to Serbia?" Have you found that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've now seen the context in which the word liberation appears twice more in the document, Mr. Savic. You've agreed that in the --

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've agreed that in the first context, I showed you, it should be read to mean or what was meant there was liberation meaning the military takeover on ethnic grounds of Bosanski Samac and the installation of a Serb-only government. That same meaning you just agreed with applies equally to those two other references to the word "liberation" in that document, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with that document for the moment. It can be left there because I may refer to it again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so when I asked you about liberation earlier, and you said in military terms it was the capture of territory, that is ground, from the enemy --

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You couldn't really describe the non-Serb Muslim and Croat majority population of Bosanski Samac in April, 1992, as the enemy, could you?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the armed part, illegally armed part. That part, not all of them, but a significant number of Muslims and Croats were armed. They were our opponents, as far as we were concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel Pedisic in the 17th headquarters command, did you know him at the time? That's P-e-d-i-s-i-c.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that man with that last name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The command of the 4th Detachment of which you were a member was sending reports to your, that is the detachment's commanding officer, Nikolic, as to what was happening on the 17th -- 16th, 17th and 18th of April, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The 17th, the 18th and the period after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And military procedure in the JNA at the time was reports of things such as civil disturbances or attempted rebellions or armed rebellions would have been or should have been sent from that level of command to the next and the one after that and the one after that and should have been sent all the way up the command; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any reports which Nikolic or the command of the 17th Tactical Group was making could only have been based upon, as far as you know, information that you, being the only soldiers, the 4th Detachment, the only JNA soldiers in Bosanski Samac, were sending them?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If there had been a clash between 3.00 and 4.00 a.m. on the morning of the 17th of April between the Territorial Defence and MUP of the Serb municipality and the SDA, TO, you would have known about it, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had there been a clash between Serb TO in Bosanski Samac and SDA TO on the morning of early hours of the morning of the 17th of April, you would have been aware of it, wouldn't you? Because of your patrols going around the town.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not the Serb TO. I knew that there was an earlier TO staff where there were a lot of superior officers there but this was earlier, when we are talking about the -- this time, this was a regular unit of the 4th Detachment. I don't know what time period you're talking about. If there had been any kind of conflict of any kind, we would be obliged to inform our superior command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of any clash between 3.00 and 4.00 in the morning of the 17th of April, 1992, between members of the Territorial Defence and MUP of the Serb municipality of Bosanski Samac, with the SDA's Territorial Defence and MUP?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember any such information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that because it didn't happen?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had it happened, I would have probably known about it, but I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would have known, based upon the information coming from your patrols in the town, of any forces coming across -- coming from the Republic of Croatia attempting an infantry attack across the bridge on the Sava River, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were certainly no forces from the Republic of Croatia attempting an infantry attack on the town of Bosanski Samac in the early hours of the morning of the 17th of April, were there?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an attempt of an attack from Prud but I told you that on the 17th, Radovan took a part of the unit out to their positions and that one of our members was wounded and that's when the shelling started from Prud and from Slavonia, from Croatia, the shelling of Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was directed to forces coming from the Republic of Croatia, not Prud, on the 17th of April, there were no forces coming from the Republic of Croatia on the 17th of April, attempting an infantry attack across the bridge, were there?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were no such forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And because?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Re you should be winding up now. You should be winding up.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There are several areas which are quite important for the Prosecution case which I wish to cover with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which were not covered with Mr. -- the previous witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Radovan Antic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Radovan Antic was the commander up until 23rd or 4th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can you indicate then how much more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Probably about an hour, I think, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, Mr. -- Because you've been cross-examining since 9.00. The Trial Chamber will give you half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I just say we received no indication of a time limit. This morning I received a telephone message a telephone call from chambers which we got at about 9.40 indicating a time limit but we had never received one before and I had prepared my topics on the basis of a reasonable time to cross-examine, not a limited time, based upon a witness who is giving very important evidence for Mr. Zaric and has done so for two hours. I was just asking if possible if I could be given a reasonable time to finish and I just don't think I can finish and do justice to the Prosecution case in half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re, the Trial Chamber is of the view that if you can concentrate on the period when this witness was the commander, because we've heard all the evidence when Radovan Antic was in -- was the commander and you did sufficient cross-examination with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: At the moment I was asking him about -- there is an error in the transcript before where it says has done so for two hours. I actually meant two days, he'd been giving evidence for two days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Re, you know very well how many hours he took.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm just correcting the transcript. I think I said two hours. I meant he had given evidence for two days, to Mr. Zaric and in cross-examination for Mr. Pantelic. That was just an error I was trying to correct there. The areas I was asking the witness about now were when he was the deputy commander on the 17th, 18th and 19th and reports which were made of what happened and the effect of what is in these reports. He was the deputy commander. It's just before the period when he was appointed commander but there are areas in which he can give evidence on which Mr. Antic wasn't cross-examined because the Prosecution had time limits there with Mr. Antic so we weren't able to go over all areas in relation to those documents so if I could possibly ask for leave for that period before the 23rd which relates directly to the takeover which the Prosecution said and this witness agrees was on an ethnic persecutory basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, but please do not keep on one point for too long like has been happening in the past.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I asked you a moment ago was about forces coming across the river and you said it didn't happen. That being so, the Territorial Defence of the Serb municipality couldn't have successfully repelled an attack that didn't happen, could it?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence of the Serb municipality did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown P19 ter?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could this be a bit magnified because we cannot read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What were you saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you read the document, Mr. Savic?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've heard the questions I've just asked you and based upon that, the information in the first sentence is, the first paragraph, is untrue, isn't it? I'm sorry, the first sentence. Not the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure that in Samac, there was no other unit other than the 4th Detachment, and that was not the TO. It was actually a unit of the JNA. This is the first time I'm seeing this document and I have no idea who is the author of this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a military document?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that, but I don't know who signed it. It was signed by a certain Pedisic whom I don't know. This is the first time that I'm seeing this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just asking you about the truth of the information contained in the document. Just accept it's a JNA military document in evidence in this trial. The first sentence is -- it's clearly incorrect, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me, it's incorrect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second sentence, where it says members of the Territorial Defence and MUP of Serb municipality took control of the MUP, the silo and the bridge, those facilities were taken over but not by those bodies; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And likewise, the sentence about the forces coming over from Republic of Croatia we've just spoken about, that too is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next sentence, sorry, the next paragraph, "A part of the Tactical Group 17 is in Bosanski Samac and the artillery have taken up positions in order to prevent anyone crossing the Sava River from the Republic of Croatia"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not have artillery as part of the detachment, not even a -- the smallest mortar of 60 millimetres. There can be no question of having any artillery. It was not there in the town, nor was it a part of my detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with that document. Sir, could you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown P23 ter?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While the document is coming, Major General Savo Jankovic, he was the commander of the 17th Corps command; is that correct, at that time, in April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible, it's possible. I didn't know those very high-ranking people. I never had an opportunity to meet them, to see them, to listen to them. I was in the reserve force. Who was occupying the top positions, I really didn't know. I did hear a couple of names but I didn't know the people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please have a look at the document and I just want to you look at the first paragraph, you can see that it's a JNA military document on its face. Have you read the first paragraph, Mr. Savic?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This purports to be a document of Major General Savo Jankovic, the command of the 17th Corps, of the 17th Corps command?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This is the first time I see this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The way that intelligence or reports worked in the JNA at that time was orders were sent, as we said before, up the command to him, and he would have received information, you would assume, upon which he would have written this report?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I never laid eyes on this document before, and the title is daily operations report, and this kind of document, I'm not talking about this specific document, but very often this kind of document would contain information delivered in a timely manner but then this information would be trimmed in the manner of speaking but I've never laid eyes on this one before and I believe I know for a fact that this is not true. It may have been the case that someone was a bit late informing whoever needed to be informed that someone from the administration section forwarded the wrong information. Whatever the case may have been this information here is not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the information that on the 18th of April, armed forces of the Republic of Croatia were not active against units within the zone of jurisdiction of the corps. Are you saying that's the information which is not accurate?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information is not accurate at least, as concerns Samac. I don't know about the other sections of the corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You turn to the second page, the paragraph that says, "On the 17th, 18th of April, Serb TO units, police and a part of the Tactical Group 17 units engaged in activities against paramilitary groups in Bosanski Samac. On 18th of April, 1992, until 1100 hours, the said forces established control or total control over Bosanski Samac." Next paragraph, "The town is peaceful, the civilian authorities are consolidating and establishing their power. Tactical Group 17 received orders to secure what had been achieved and not to continue with offensive steps." You've read that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't really find my feet because you read very fast. I wasn't able to find it. I can't find that particular section of the text, the one which you've just read out. Item 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, which item are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's in item 3, and it should be the third paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 17th April. Yes, 3. On 17 April, Serb forces, Serb TO units, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, right, yes, yes, I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've read that? Have you read that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the next paragraph that says, "The town is peaceful, civilian authorities are consolidating and establishing their power. Tactical Group 17 received orders to secure what had been achieved and not to continue with offensive steps."

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me, this is simply not true, because we did not take part in any activities whatsoever apart from occupying the perimeter of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, it says "To secure what had been achieved." Secure may mean leave in place what has been achieved, guard the perimeters of the town and not interfere with the paramilitary takeover.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can mean that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the takeover, the JNA participated in the collection of weapons from people in the municipality of Bosanski Samac. You've already testified as to that occurring.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct me if I'm wrong, but I think you said that Mr. Zaric and Mr. Tadic were entrusted with supervising the collection of weapons in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, in addition to other people. There were other people who had the same task but they stayed at the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was a sensitive job and it had to be done properly according to the orders you received?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as the deputy commander, you and Mr. Antic would only or were only prepared to trust this sensitive and important task to people you trusted to do the job properly?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't personally take part -- or participate in collecting the weapons yourself; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did -- where were Mr. Tadic and Mr. Zaric ordered to take the weapons that had been given up by the citizens to?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their task was to record all the weapons collected and to take it to the TO warehouse, which was at the TO headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they ordered to give receipts to people they had taken the weapons from?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know --

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They merely had to record the serial number of the rifle. I'm not sure what they wrote down eventually but their orders were to control this activity, to monitor the course of the activity. I remember that Miroslav Tadic was entrusted with a task, along side with someone else helping him, to record all the weapons, to draw up lists, and take the weapons to the storage, to the warehouse at the TO HQ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was an order you gave -- the command gave to them -- that you gave to them after receiving it from Nikolic after he had informed you that he was aware that the Crisis Staff had participated in the takeover, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, the effect of collecting weapons from anyone who may have had them in Bosanski Samac, the effect of that was to prevent anyone attempting to organise against the new government and new authorities controlling Samac, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know is that by doing that, by performing that activity, we had a number of people who were in charge of military tasks from the detachment, now whether this made it possible for organs of authority, for bodies of authority to continue functioning normally, that is a political issue. Perhaps so but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The answer that the witness gave was not properly recorded in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that the witness said that the main task was to prevent people to shoot on their own personal -- for members of the detachment, and this is not the way I see it recorded here in the transcript. Said we had a number of people who were in charge of military tasks from the detachment. But it doesn't make much sense, yes it's obvious that they had a lot of soldiers in the detachment but not -- the real meaning of the answer was not recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the witness repeat his answer? Slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Collection of weapons was performed for the personal safety of people from the detachment who had been deployed along the lines of defence, to prevent people from a house in whatever situation in possession of weapons to endanger the people deployed along the lines, and we didn't know or we were not willing to secure the proper functioning of authorities in such a way that we were not really in favour of and they didn't favour us much either. It's possible that it happened by virtue of that very fact. I'm not really an expert in that point, in the political point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is the -- you've agreed that the effect of the JNA's inaction was to allow the paramilitaries to consolidate their takeover of the town. That was an order not to interfere. In tandem with that, Nikolic ordered you to order Tadic and Zaric or whoever to collect weapons, to go through the town collecting weapons. The effect of these two orders together, don't interfere but collect weapons, was to assist the paramilitaries and the Crisis Staff in the takeover or sorry in their consolidation of power in Bosanski Samac immediately after the night of the 16th of April, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's your opinion. I will repeat: The purpose of the detachment, I've said it over 100 times here, should I have a go at that again? We didn't have anything -- we didn't know that this or that government would come. We simply carried out our tasks as they were ordered to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not my question. My question is as to the effect based on what you saw and what you've agreed to already, what you've testified about already, the effect of those two orders or non-orders, don't interfere but collect weapons was that the JNA, the 4th Detachment, whether it wanted to or not, was assisting consolidation of power by the Crisis Staff and the paramilitaries in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, I see that because that's what it looked like. We did not know about that previously but we did as we were ordered to do.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please be asked to repeat the last part of his answer a bit more distinctly?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just repeat the last part of your answer? The interpreters didn't hear it. More clearly.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps by carrying out our orders, perhaps I say, we did make it possible in that way to make possible for the organs of authority or bodies of authority to do their job. Perhaps. Let me say. That was not part of the order. The only thing that was in the order is not to interfere and to stick to our job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified about a meeting at Pelagicevo on about, not the precise date, but about the 22nd of May, 1992, at which Colonel Djurdjevic gave a positively-received speech after he'd been appointed the commander. You said Mr. Zaric was there, you said Mr. Simic was there, and Mr. Todorovic was there. Was Mr. Tadic there? That's Mr. Miroslav Tadic. Was he there too?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as I remember, no, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, Mr. Pantelic, and I think Mr. Lazarevic -- sorry, Mr. Pisarevic as well, asked you about the JNA and Mr. Pisarevic specifically asked you about its structure and when you -- when you joined the VRS. Do you remember that testimony over the last couple of days?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was first in the reserve force of the army, until 1997, and then I was transferred into active military service. I'm really not sure what you're asking me. Was I in the army? Was I not in the army? When was I in the army?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked about what you did in 1992 and -- 1992 following the dissolution of the Federal -- Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the transformation of the JNA in Bosnia into the VRS, and you going from one into the other and the changing of the names of the brigades following the transfer from the JNA to the VRS. That's what I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The question is a bit enigmatic to me, I must admit but I'll try to answer that. The Army of Republika Srpska was established on the 12th of May, 1992. Up until the war broke out in Samac, I had been a member of a unit in Derventa, also the JNA, but that was a war unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you this. I was just referring to what you said before so I could ask you something, to direct your mind back to the questions you were asked.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please ask this question again, if you can? But keep it brief. The questions are too long, I can no longer keep track.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Re, can we get on track? We are taking too much time on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Only in fairness to the witness was I taking him back to his previous answer so I could direct him there rather than go through it all again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The evidence is already on record. He has explained how he moved from one army to the next, to the next post. So all you do is put the question you want to put to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll do that. I'm just trying to remind him of it so we don't go backwards and forwards over the whole thing again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, what I'm simply asking you is: After you lost -- after you were removed from the command in 1992, your evidence was you carried out the duties of a clerk in the training and operations department. What did you do? What were your precise duties? And where were you based?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed in Samac as a clerk for general affairs, in the detachment which later became the 5th Battalion until the 1st of September, 1992. From the 1st of September, I was transferred to Pelagicevo, to the brigade command, to work there as clerk for the training and operations department. I stayed in that post for many years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question was: What were your precise duties? What did you do when you were working as a training and operations clerk? What did your job entail? What did you do every day?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about the brigade or the battalion? I was not the clerk for general affairs in the brigade. That was in a lower ranking unit, in a battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992 and 1993, when you were working as a clerk, all I'm asking you is what did you do? What were your duties? What did you do every day?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, are you talking about the battalion or the brigade?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I think we can just clear this up a little bit quickly if we say, as in the witness's answer, he was the clerk for general affairs in the 4th Detachment which later became the 5th Battalion, until the 1st of September, 1992. So we could hear from you, Mr. Savic, what you did until the 1st of September, 1992, and then after the 1st of September, you went to the brigade command in Pelagicevo - sorry. I didn't pronounce it correctly - and that's where you were clerk of the training and operations. You have the two jobs. Maybe you can explain what you did in the first job, what did you in the second job.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As clerk for general affairs in the 4th Detachment, which was later battalion, I kept records for all members, records of woundings, of members getting killed, family visits. We organised, also that was part of my remit for the burials. We would go and see the families of our wounded members, to hospitals. I mainly organised these things. I didn't travel much. I mostly stayed put. I'd always find friends or acquaintances who had their own vehicle who could go and make the visits, convey our greetings, so those were general affairs within the administration. And that's what I did as clerk in the battalion. Then the brigade, I was clerk for operations and training. My duty was to do everything as ordered of my direct superior, who this time was the Chief of Staff, because I was at the staff of the brigade, which implies the command. I kept records again, duty rosters, training plans, training programmes, with young soldiers, recruits, sometimes I was the trainer, I performed the training, I would visit the front lines, the soldiers, the trenches, again, I kept records as to who and when got hurt, what the enemy operations were and so on and so forth. There was a lot to be done. We were two or three people working on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you responsible for ordering or the purchase of any equipment?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said something a bit earlier about compensation. When you were working as the training and operations clerk and the general clerk, how were you being paid?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Salary in times of war was insignificant. It was merely symbolic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you receiving a salary?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A very small sum. We almost would have been better off getting no money at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The salary you were receiving was being paid by the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, that's Serbia and Montenegro, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We, members of the army who were never part of Yugoslavia's army, that is, we were not active-duty, as we call it, reserve officers and the army from the area, we were receiving a small remuneration which was almost no money at all. Only those officers who were from Yugoslavia received their salaries, their remunerations and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying there were officers from Yugoslavia working with you after -- in November -- sorry, in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Officers of Yugoslavia left Bosnia and Herzegovina before the 19th of May, and only the people who had been born there stayed. Officers when had been JNA officers previously but they now stayed in our army, the Army of Republika Srpska. They were receiving some sort of financial compensation or remuneration but I don't know exactly what it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, with the -- when you were -- I'm sorry, following, from mid-April through to mid-May, when the VRS was formed, you said the 12th of May, the JNA remained in and your detachment remained in Bosanski Samac, didn't it? It's a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It didn't withdraw or place itself under the authority of the government of the Republic of Bosnia or disband, that is, your JNA unit, did it?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. It didn't disband. It stayed there. And very quickly it was called the battalion. It wasn't a detachment any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It certainly didn't place itself under the authority of the government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina between mid-April and the 12th of May, did it?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's 12.30, Your Honour. I am almost finished, I can assure you of that. There are just several areas I need to cover.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we'll take our break and continue at 12.50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, you will be pleased to know I have no further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, counsel? Any other counsel before the final re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, my learned friend is finished with his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: He is, thank you so much. Your Honour, could I have just a few seconds to get my papers and to place myself there? Because of the communication with the bench and with the witness? I'm thinking to facilitate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you can move.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Further cross-examination by Mr. Pantelic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Savic?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are seeing each other again today. My learned friend the Prosecutor asked you today about the role of the 4th Detachment in the tasks -- about their tasks and you answered about this in detail to me, to my colleague, Mr. Lazarevic, to the Prosecutor. I just wanted to ask you something briefly about that. The 4th Detachment, as part of the 17th Tactical Group, and the JNA, acted on behalf of what state?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On behalf of the state of Republika Srpska. This is what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can we clarify when?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, the period being covered.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've heard the Prosecutor. Could you please tell us when?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the 12th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're talking about, to be precise, it was no longer the 4th Detachment but it was the 5th battalion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 5th battalion, as part of the 2nd Posavina Brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But the 4th Detachment was established by order of the commander of the 17th Tactical Group in January, 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: As I understand it, the re-examination or the re-cross, for Mr. Simic is limited to matters arising from the cross-examination that affect the interests of Mr. Pantelic's client. He asked these questions in his own cross-examination. Nothing so far has popped up in the last few moments which to me any way seems to have -- relate to something affecting the interests of his client. Otherwise we will be here for a long, long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will clarify that. I am just trying to find out because it was some misunderstanding when my learned friend intervened with regard to the time period of 4th Detachment so that was the question I would like to clarify. My line of questions is based on the fact that we have to establish here a clear evidences and basis what was the role of my client, Dr. Blagoje Simic, in the events, allegedly in the charges in the indictment, where the subparagraph, subcharge 1 of Count 1 of the indictment is forcible takeover. The position of the Defence of Dr. Blagoje Simic is that he was not in any sense connected to the military operations issues or other acts of 4th Detachment, 17th Tactical Group, JNA, volunteers, Serbian police, et cetera, et cetera. So in order to properly present the defence of my client, Dr. Blagoje Simic, I have to establish inter alia on behalf of which entity 4th Detachment acted in the period of January 1992 up to the 19th of May of 1992. So this fact is of the importance for the Defence of my client and that is the reason why I'm asking very simple question of this witness, to get his response on behalf of which entity or state or institution acted, 4th Detachment acted in the period between the date of his establishment of formation up to 19th of May, 1992, in order to precisely get a position of my client in all these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Mr. Pantelic of course won't object if the Prosecution then tenders into evidence the Security Council resolutions and the general assembly resolutions relating to the and made the order to or the call to immediately disband the JNA on Bosnian territory as of April, mid-April, 1992. He won't object to me tendering Security Council resolutions saying there should be disbanded, withdrawn, or subordinated to the government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Is that what's coming from this? That I should be allowed to reopen to do that? This has already been covered.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This is a fact witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What I'm trying to say here is that you did put questions to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before the cross-examination of the Prosecution, and most of what you're trying to say here was covered during that period. So this is not a time to repeat what you did then. This is a time to only ask questions of this witness on something that has not been covered or that was raised during the cross-examination of the Prosecution which pertains to the role of your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That is exactly my point and if you allow me to ask a question, you will see that that's the basis of my line of questioning, please. Can I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, the 4th Detachment of the 17th Tactical Group, in the period from January, 1992, until May, 1992, acted on behalf of whom? On whose behalf did you act?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On behalf of the Yugoslav People's Army with the aim of preserving the then Republic of Yugoslavia, up until that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you operating on behalf of the Serb municipality and Pelagicevo under formation and on behalf of the Crisis Staff of that municipality?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We existed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you act in their name?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is all I wanted to ask you. Nothing more than that. The Crisis Staff of the Serbian Municipality of Samac and Pelagicevo, did it ever issue you any order to act on behalf of the Serbian Municipality of Samac and Pelagicevo in the period that you existed as the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you today or he tried to construct something about your personal position on the indictments against certain leaders of the SDS. He mentioned Mr. Karadzic, Mr. Krajisnik, Mrs. Plavsic and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Don't answer. I object. I didn't and Your Honour stopped me going down that track which I wasn't going to go down any way. This doesn't arise. He said he respected the work of the Tribunal. I said these people had been indicted. Bang. I wasn't asking for his opinion nor trying to construct anything in relation to his opinion of those indictments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's when the Trial Chamber stopped that line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I wasn't going there but yes, I was stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: He already answered so I'd like to move to strike all these portions -- all this part of the transcript, of this morning, relating to that or otherwise I just have one question with regard to that, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, just go ahead with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Savic, are you familiar with the fact that there are no judgements of this Tribunal against Karadzic, Krajisnik and the other SDS leaders?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know only about Mrs. Biljana Plavsic, I don't know about the others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, if you want to be allowed to ask this witness questions, you have to deal with what I've directed you to deal with, matters concerning your client, which arose from the Prosecution's cross-examination only.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, could you please tell me when you were discussing the document P127 this morning, this is the document with the 13 signatories, could you please tell the Trial Chamber, if you know, what was the basis for the arrest of a number of people in those initial few days after the 17th of April, 1992? What was the -- what were these people suspected of so that they were arrested?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which people are you thinking of?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm thinking of the Muslims and Croats in Samac.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do I personally think about that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, not what you personally think about that but what were the suspicions based on which they were arrested?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was because most probably they were Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any information about whether they were in possession of any weapons or whether any proceedings were initiated against them regarding this matter?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A number of them did possess weapons. I know this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you today about the percentage of Serbs in the municipality of Samac and you said that before the -- before 1992, based on the 1991 census, there were fewer than 50 per cent of Serbs in Bosanski Samac. You remember you talked about that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that the Serbs were in a minority?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I wasn't sure. I think that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm interested in now, since you've already replied to this question, and I would like to clarify this because of the transcript, and for the Trial Chamber, when the municipality of Samac was practically divided into two parts, into the Serb municipality of Samac and the Samac-Domaljevac part which was part of the Federation, the Serbian part of the municipality, in that part, were the Serbs in a majority or in a minority? So I'm talking about the Serbian part of the pre-war municipality of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the events, Domaljevac was no longer part of our municipality, with a large number of villages and a large number of Croats which means that in the municipality of Samac, the larger -- the Serbs were left in a minority. There was a greater number of Serbs left in that part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecutor in the -- his formulations which correspond to his view of this case, talked to you about the establishment of the new regime based on discriminatory foundations in Samac and so on. So now I would like to ask you, first, before the 17th of April, 1992, were all the three peoples in Bosanski Samac constitutive peoples, Croats, Muslims and Serbs?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, before you go on, just to clarify the answer of Mr. Savic which is on page 75, line 8 to line 11, I think for the sake of clarity, you need to ask the question again, because the answer has not -- as transcribed, makes little or even no sense. As you can see if you just read through it. I won't bother quoting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I will clarify that. Thank you, Your Honour, for your assistance and intervention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because of the transcript, the precision of the transcript I would like to ask you this question and could you please respond to that? The pre-war -- and when I say the pre-war, I'm talking about the municipality before the 17th of April, 1992, the pre-war territory of the municipality of Bosanski Samac was divided, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wait, wait, please just take your time?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean divided?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wait, wait, please. We were talking over the past few days about the formation of Samac-Domaljevac within the federation and here in Republika Srpska, the municipality of Samac remained so you remember what we were talking about?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please could you wait until I finish? You said before this Chamber, Domaljevac, Prud and all of these things remained in the Federation. Please listen to what I'm asking you. We have a territory of the municipality of Bosanski Samac before the 17th of April, 1992. As part of that territory, that territory includes Samac, Domaljevac, Prud; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 17th of April, since the military front was already being formed in the surrounding area, the territory of Bosanski Samac was divided, is that so?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was a second municipality then formed called Samac-Domaljevac which was under the control of the Croat authorities?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also Prud was not under the control of the Serbian municipality; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My direct question to you is: What remained of that municipality, this Serb municipality? Were the Serbs in a majority or a minority on that territory?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in a majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: This is just historically factually wrong. What my learned friend is putting to the witness. There was a municipality with a democratically elected government in force as of the 17th of April, 1992. There is no evidence before this Trial Chamber that there was a divided Serb municipality or the government of a Serb municipality in Bosanski Samac, democratically elected according to the constitution of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia or the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. And my questions were not directed to that. My questions were directed to the ethnic division, demographic division of the municipality of Bosanski Samac as constituted by the legitimate government of Bosnia, the Socialist Republic, within the democratically elected boundaries. Not this other stuff. I don't know where this is coming from.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we have plenty of evidence, Your Honour, may I explain just -- we have plenty of evidence before this Trial Chamber that the pre-war territory of municipality of Bosanski Samac were divided as of 17th of April, 1992, and up to now, according to the Dayton Peace Accord and all other regulations, still is divided. Two municipalities. One part of the municipality is related to Muslim Croat Federation the other for the Serb side. So when my learned friend asked this witness to say where the Serbs were majority or minority in municipality of Bosanski Samac, I just want to know on which part, because evidently, as of 17th of April, 1992, we have two parts, we have two separate municipalities, of Bosanski Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, my questions were only before the 17th, not afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I'm trying to say. The question related to the period before the takeover.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In that case, in that case, I can agree with the fact that the Serbs were less than 50 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Savic, could you please tell me, now we are talking about the period before the 17th of April, 1992, was there also under 50 per cent of the Croats, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the percentage of Muslims, approximately, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were Muslims only in the town of Samac itself. There were no Muslims living in the areas around the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your personal knowledge, since we are talking about the ratio of Muslims, of Croats and Serbs, prior to the outbreak of the conflict in the municipality of Bosanski Samac, what was the ratio of Muslims and Croats in relation to Serbs in the social life, decision-making, in company policies and so on, what is your information?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're talking about the period before the war?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately before the war, I'm talking about 1992 now.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the arrival of national parties to power, there were divisions that came about. There was separation. Everybody wished to state that they were a Muslim, a Serb or a Croat and so on. What I'm trying to say is that these relations were tense, which up until then were, let's say, all right. So these relations were somewhat disrupted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When we are talking about all of this, at the time, did you have information about -- at the time on the 17th of April, 1992, that there was a municipal -- a Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that, yes, and I even said --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. Just tell me whether you heard of it or not. Please don't explain anything.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these relations between the ethnic groups --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, I will take care of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, please, no long expanded answer, just say yes, no, I remember, I don't remember, so that we can speed things up, and please take it slowly. The last question regarding this topic: Your personal knowledge about this, the Serbs in the municipality of Samac, were they allied together with the Muslims against Croats? Were they allied with Croats against the Muslims or what were these divisions like? Could you please give me your explanation, your assessment of these interethnic relations before the 17th of 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in his examination-in-chief sufficiently. I think we are wasting time going over this again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I agree. I will move on, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the Prosecutor asked you about this information, this is document P127, with the 13 signatories, and he concluded that you were criticising the civilian authorities here for the persecution, so I'm asking you directly: In your opinion, and based on your knowledge, if there were certain acts of persecution, do you ascribe that to the civilian authorities or to some other bodies?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say civilian authorities, do you mean the police and the volunteers or do you mean the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the Serb police was mostly involved in this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecutor then asked you about the terms paramilitary, parapolice and so on and you provided your explanations based on the way you think that it was. I'm asking you as an experienced officer, a man who has a certain level of education, if there were a written order of the military command to members of the paramilitary units, as you say, I'm thinking specifically of Lugar, Crni and the others, how would you define that? Would they still be members of the paramilitary or would they have any kind of role now? Could you please explain that to the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I were to receive such an order, but I did not, we didn't get it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no, stop, stop. You didn't understand me. If you as commander of the 4th Detachment were to give a combat order or an order to Lugar, Crni and the others whom you described as members of the paramilitary, would they then become regular soldiers as part of the -- otherwise why would you issue the order at all? So could you please explain that in this context? If you were to issue an order to them?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The question doesn't make sense at all. Besides your asking the witness to speculate. Move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Specifically Mr. Savic on the basis of your knowledge as a reserve officer?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm going to another topic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have spoken about paramilitaries and parapolice when asked by the Prosecution you provided your opinion, your view?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question now is: Did you know that members of those paramilitary units, Lugar, Crni and the rest of them, received any orders from the superior command, that is the 17th Tactical Group, please just say what you know about that if you know anything?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they never received any orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Furthermore, page 41 of today's transcript, lines 12 through 17, the Prosecutor asked you about the roles of certain commanders about the military doctrine. My question now is: The military commander, does he act, does he assess the situation, or does he wait for orders from the superior command in a situation, in an emergency? Can you please just explain what happens in that case. What's the role of the military commander on the ground?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He assesses the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Rephrase the question because even it is not clear enough to me, what means military commander? On what level? On the level of a unit on the level of a brigade, of the level of an army or what level? Because it makes sense to me that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic, if you actually go back to what you're referring to on page 41, lines 12 through 17, I think the answer of Mr. Savic is quite clear. He's talking about the commander of the Tactical Group, and I think he's talking -- the commander of the Tactical Group, that level, an officer of the same level, and then he goes on to say he's authorised to make a decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: And then he goes on and says when he's faced with a situation where he has to take a decision on his own, with his assistants, then he informs the superior command and maybe appeals for assistance or help or advice. I think the answer is perfectly clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Regarding two, yes, Your Honour, regarding to the 17th Tactical Group but now my question is focused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I beg to differ, Mr. Pantelic. He talks about the commander of the Tactical Group, that level, an officer of the same level, implying in other command groups. At least that's my interpretation of Mr. Savic's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've heard what Judge Williams said. I want to know if the same applies to the command of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's a lower level, without authority to make important decisions, unless people deployed along the lines are in danger. Then certain steps can be taken to remedy the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Further, you were asked by the Prosecutor today about certain moments of an operation, what they refer to as the attack on Samac, by a number of military and paramilitary groups. The defence takes the opposite view. Tell me please, you said there was no Serbian TO, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your assistant, Simo Zaric, for you was a reliable person, someone you trusted, and he had valid information; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He had his own channels, intelligence channels, up and down the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By all means, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had no reason to doubt his assessment or the information he provided?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No reason at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had no reason to doubt the judgement of Commander Nikolic, commander of the 17th Tactical Group who had all the information coming in from the ground and who would then provide his own assessment?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was at least the way it was supposed to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, Exhibit number P16, it's a videotape, an interview released to Novi Sad TV. Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic states the following. It's page 2 of the transcript. "Well over the last three or four days, we have been engaged in combat with members of the 1st Brigade of the ZNG. After their attempt to break into Bosanski Samac and after they were shattered by the Serbian TO." Specifically what I want to know now, if Commander Nikolic claims that, and he is your superior after all, what did he mean by Serbian TO? What did he refer to? How did he arrive at that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps you should be asking him that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That was going over the interpretation. Can you repeat what you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise. I believe that it was a purely asking for speculation of this witness, what Colonel Nikolic meant by saying that -- using these particular words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, what Mr. Pantelic is asking the witness is -- because Nikolic is mentioned the Serbian TO, which the witness had said, the Serbian TO did not exist at that time. So he wants to find out from the witness how come Commander Nikolic mentioned the Serbian TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Maybe we will just wait for redirect of ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe to speed this up a little. You have no reason to doubt that Colonel Nikolic was lying nor telling the truth when he was saying this?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He can say whatever he likes but not that that's something that I should know. You should ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Clarification on the transcript, it says you have no reason to doubt that he was lying nor telling the truth. It's a contradiction. Maybe it wasn't interpreted. Maybe the translation went astray.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will repeat that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Savic, I've just read out to you what the colonel said?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll repeat this. What I've just read out to you, the statement by Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to doubt the truth or rather the authenticity of his words?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe -- I don't know which TO he was speaking about. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Likewise, Simo Zaric in that same interview, P16, we are talking about the videotape transcript, page 3, stated the following: "All operational information over the last couple of days indicates that this town and this people are in for something, for a disaster." You do agree with this, don't you?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It goes on to state the following: "It is in that framework that the 4th Detachment of the Territorial Defence prepared for something like that. And all I can say on the basis of the documents that we have, after the war operations in this town, it only would have taken three or four hours for the HOS members and for the Green Berets to take the town and to transform it into a war-torn town, to massacre the Serbs and the Muslims in the town, who worked together to establish this Territorial Defence." You do agree with what Simo Zaric said?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, but without the TO bit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean? What's wrong with the TO?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand this TO. TO? This was no such thing as TO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is something that your assistant for security said?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he can say whatever he likes but that's the only slight bit that I do not agree with. The rest is okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, can we stop here? We have some procedural matters to deal with.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the witness be led out of the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, the Trial Chamber would like to continue with the Rule 92 bis statements already submitted. Regarding those submitted on behalf of Mr. Miroslav Tadic, that is Exhibit 184/3, by Mr. Djordje Tubakovic, that will be admitted under seal. However, paragraphs 11 to 14, which discuss the acts and conduct of the accused are struck off. Paragraph 9 is also struck off as irrelevant. In paragraph 19, from the sentence beginning "I know that until he was arrested," up to the end of that paragraph is also struck off. In paragraph 21, the last words, "Nor was such an order ever issued" are struck off. And in paragraph 22, the first two sentences, which discuss the acts and conduct of the accused are also struck off. This witness will come and give viva voce testimony in closed session for 40 minutes dealing with the matters raised in those paragraphs which are struck off. He will be open to cross-examination, also limited to the same time of 40 minutes. The next statement is that by Stojan Damjanovic which is Exhibit 185/3. Paragraphs 7 to 11 will be struck off. Otherwise, the statement is admitted into evidence. This witness will also come to give viva voce testimony for half an hour on those paragraphs that are struck off and cross-examination will also be limited to half an hour. The statements submitted on behalf of Mr. Simo Zaric, Exhibit D43/4 by Niko Pavic, paragraphs 27, 28, are struck off, as well as the last sentence of paragraph 23. The rest of the statement is admitted into evidence. There will be no cross-examination. The statement D45/4, by Mato Antunovic is a character witness. It will be admitted into evidence except that paragraphs 24 and 34 -- paragraphs 23 and paragraph 34 will be struck off. This witness will not be cross-examined. The next statement is Exhibit D46/4, the statement of Dzemo Jasenica. This statement is admitted except for paragraph 28 which is struck off. There will be no cross-examination. The next statement is D47/4, by Stevan Nikolic. Paragraphs 30 and 32, and paragraphs 39, 41, 42, and 44 are struck off, and the first sentence of paragraph 40 is also struck off. I'll repeat that so that it's clear. It's paragraphs 30, 32, 39, 41, 42 and 44, and the first sentence of paragraph 40, that are struck off. The witness will come and give viva voce testimony for 40 minutes. Cross-examination will be allowed for one hour. The statement of Nizam Ramusovic, we don't have a number for it yet. Perhaps we can have a number now for identification purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, it was a draft statement. It wasn't signed. So this was the reason why we don't have a number for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because you had said that you wanted an indication so that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and then according to the ruling, we could organise the certification of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
